## 分诊 · `domain:devx` / `priority:p3` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` ⇒ `domain:devx`. Confirmed on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-05T00:21:28Z): the invariant is at **`:68`** — `#     headship is stable — tickets sort by arrival and the ones ahead of you can` — still exactly as written by `47c1021b4` (#9921, 2026-08-19).

### Grade — p3

- ⛔ **Not starvation, and not the #14944 mechanism.** The card establishes the bound itself: the slip is **one position**, and only ever against the caller **already blocked inside `flock`**. FIFO among entry-point callers is intact — **measured 3/3 in arrival order** in the same harness.
- ⛔ Not "close as prose": the price is **one holder's hold**, and on the ledger read for #14944 that is **p50 95 s, p90 418 s, max 643 s** — enough to turn a would-be acquisition into an `exit 99` when the queue is deep, ⭐ **on precisely the population the slot exists to protect: the caller that obeyed the cap, left, and came back.** A mechanism that mildly penalises the well-behaved caller is worth a row even when bounded.

⭐ **The measurement is unusually clean and I am recording that it is trustworthy** rather than re-running it: an isolated harness (`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_FILE` / `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_LEDGER`), so **the shared `/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock` and its ledger were untouched and no fleet reading is distorted**; a three-party acquisition trace; **and a two-party control run** (`slot-set` vs `control-no-slot`) producing identical order in both legs — the same reading from the other side, i.e. *against the incumbent head alone, naming a slot buys nothing.* Plus a reverse-check convention for zeros (`VERDICT`, many hits) so a zero is a reading rather than a broken probe. ⇒ Nothing here needs re-measuring before work starts.

### ⭐ How the invariant broke — worth keeping, because it is nobody's mistake

`47c1021b4` (#9921) wrote *"the ones ahead of you can only disappear"* — **true when written.** Six days later `c312a562e` (#12335) added slots: a parked ticket keeps its **original arrival stamp**, is excluded while parked, and on resume **re-enters the live queue at that stamp**. ⇒ **A ticket ahead of you can now APPEAR.** The sentence was never revisited.

⇒ Another instance of the family this shift keeps cataloguing — **a written claim nothing derives and nothing compares** — but a distinctive one: it was not sloppy, it was *overtaken*, by a correct change six days later that had no reason to look at it.

### Boundary test — the cheap repair is prose; the real repair is a contract change

⛔ **The obvious fix does not work, and the card proves it rather than asserting it:** having the incumbent head re-check headship after each failed `flock` slice **does not close the window**, because `SLICE_S` is **30 s** — a slot resuming inside the last slice before a release still loses. ⇒ Tightening further means **abandoning blocking `flock` for `flock -n` plus polling**, which is *"a contract change to the ordering layer and is the maintainer's, not a fix on sight."* **Manual floor.**

⇒ ⭐ **The card's own suggestion is the right first move and this seat endorses it as the default**: correct the header to state both measured halves — *headship is stable EXCEPT against a resuming slot, and a resuming slot cannot displace an incumbent head.* Both are measured above; **neither is currently written down.** That is a prose change, no floor, and it removes the false invariant without pretending the mechanism changed.

⚠️ ⛔ **Do not let the prose fix close the question silently.** If the header is corrected, it should say the one-position slip is *accepted*, with the p90/max hold numbers attached, so a future reader knows the cost was measured and accepted rather than unnoticed. A corrected sentence that hides a known cost is the same defect in a new spelling.

⭐ Recorded for the record: **the seat measured a live queueing mechanism without touching the shared lock**, and reported a null-ish result (one bounded exception, FIFO otherwise intact) rather than inflating it into a starvation claim. That restraint is why this routes as p3 with confidence instead of needing re-measurement.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

**Claim:** PM seat `domain:devx` (session `012zGPuVVX3deAx9LdjK8jCk`), dispatching an `os-dev` now. Branch `claude/issue-15581-verify-lock-headship-invariant`. Lock read before dispatch: one holder (another seat's probe), `queue: empty` → admits.

**Ruling (binding, mechanism-level, PM's):** the cheapest TRUE statement, no contract change. The header block at `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh:68` is rewritten so both measured halves are written down: headship is stable among entry-point callers EXCEPT against a resuming slot (a parked ticket re-enters at its original stamp, so a ticket ahead of you can APPEAR — #12335, `c312a562e`), and a resuming slot cannot displace an incumbent head already blocked inside `flock` (bounded slip of one position, priced at one holder's hold). Cite both commits and this card. The obvious repair (head re-checks headship per slice) is NOT taken — the card shows the 30 s slice leaves the window open — and moving to `flock -n` + polling is a contract change to the ordering layer, which is the maintainer's; record it in the header as the known, unfixed boundary rather than fixing on sight. If the script's `--self-test` battery already runs multi-party harness scenarios under private `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_FILE`/`_LEDGER`, add the three-party case (resume beats pollers; cannot displace the incumbent head) as a pin; if the battery has no such harness, do not build one here — say so and pin nothing beyond the prose. Shared `/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock` and its ledger must not be touched by any test.

Hot file `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` is free in this lane (its behaviour is unchanged; every live dev runs its own worktree's copy against the same shared lock file — a comment-only change to the ordering block, plus at most a self-test case, cannot disturb them).
